biggest_catch: You let Duke Energy adjust your thermostat a few times per month during peak demand — free participation, but your comfort settings get nudged.
catches: You must enroll an eligible smart thermostat (your own qualifying device or a Duke-provided one) in EnergyWise Home.
Temporary peak-demand thermostat adjustments occur a few times per month; you keep override ability per program terms.
Duke states the $150 as a bill credit after successful enrollment but does not publish an exact payout timeline — s3 marked false rather than guessed.
Staying enrolled keeps the program benefits; unenrolling ends future credits.
If you buy a new thermostat to qualify, that purchase is a condition, not an upfront fee.

steps: Check that your smart thermostat is on Duke Energy's eligible-device list (or get one that is).
Install it, connect it to Wi-Fi, and register it with the manufacturer.
Go to the official Duke Energy EnergyWise Home smart thermostat page and enroll.
Allow the temporary peak-demand adjustments during the season.
Receive your $150 bill credit after successful enrollment; Duke does not publish the exact posting timeline.
